ds: Abuse of correspondent banking relationships, including nested or downstream use of a respondent's account by other institutions, to move illicit funds across borders with limited visibility of the underlying customers and purposes. Payable-through accounts and shell bank links add risk.

src.t: FATF, Guidance on Correspondent Banking Services (2016)
Wolfsberg Group, Correspondent Banking Due Diligence Questionnaire (CBDDQ) (current version, specify year)
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Guidelines: Sound management of risks related to money laundering and financing of terrorism (2014, rev. 2020)

rat: Respondent and nested bank/PSP flows via correspondent accounts over SWIFT.

ind.cx: Respondent provides access to its account for other banks or payment firms (nesting) without disclosure.
ind.fp: Group and agency arrangements are disclosed normally.
ind.ds: Respondent provides access to its account for other banks or payment firms (nesting) without disclosure.

ind.n: Respondent based in high-risk jurisdiction with weak AML supervision
ind.cx: Respondent operates where regulation or supervision is weak.
ind.fp: Large regional banks in higher-risk countries serve real trade.
ind.ds: Funds, counterparties or institutions are located in jurisdictions with weak AML supervision, sanctions exposure or limited VASP regulation.
ind.cn: Counterparty or flows in higher-risk jurisdictions with weak AML controls

ind.n: Transaction volumes disproportionate to respondent's size
ind.cx: Flows far exceed expected levels for the respondent's balance sheet or footprint.
ind.ds: Flows far exceed expected levels for the respondent's balance sheet or footprint.

ind.n: Missing or poor-quality payment message information
ind.cx: Messages lack originator or beneficiary data or use unclear references.
ind.ds: Payment messages omit, truncate or use generic placeholder data for originator or beneficiary details.
ind.cn: Missing, incomplete or placeholder originator and beneficiary information

ind.n: Pooled flows with frequent round-sum payments
ind.cx: Large round-value payments or repeated amounts for multiple unrelated beneficiaries.
ind.ds: Large round-value payments or repeated amounts for multiple unrelated beneficiaries.

ind.n: Respondent refuses or delays information requests
ind.cx: Slow, evasive or incomplete responses to RFIs.
ind.ds: Customer or counterparty delays, refuses or gives incomplete or evasive responses to KYC, refresh or request-for-information enquiries.
ind.cn: Refusal or delay in answering due diligence requests

ind.n: Links to shell banks or unlicensed entities
ind.cx: Respondent has relationships with shell or unlicensed institutions.
ind.ds: Respondent has relationships with shell or unlicensed institutions.

ind.n: Payable-through account use by respondent's customers
ind.cx: Respondent's customers transact directly through the account.
ind.ds: Underlying customers of another party transact directly through payable-through, pooled or payment-agent facilities.
ind.cn: Payable-through or pooled access enabling third-party payments

ind.n: Adverse media or enforcement on respondent
ind.cx: Respondent has regulatory action, sanctions or ML scandals.
ind.ds: Counterparties, suppliers, respondents or controllers appear in adverse media, law-enforcement notices or intelligence connected to financial crime, abuse, forced labour or organised crime.
ind.cn: Adverse media or intelligence linking counterparties to criminal activity

ctl.n: Correspondent respondent due diligence and risk rating
ctl.ds: Assesses respondent banks' jurisdiction, ownership, regulation, products and AML controls at onboarding using questionnaires and risk rating, including counterparty bank review. It sets the basis for correspondent relationships.
Requires respondents to disclose and approve downstream institutions and detects payment patterns that imply undeclared nested use. It limits exposure to unknown third-tier clients.

ctl.n: Periodic respondent review and volume monitoring
ctl.ds: Reviews respondent activity against expected volumes, updates expected activity and restricts routing via higher-risk banks. It keeps correspondent risk assessments current after onboarding.

ctl.n: Senior management approval and risk acceptance
ctl.ds: Requires named senior management or a committee to approve onboarding, continuation or waivers for higher-risk relationships, with documented mitigations and periodic re-approval. It adds accountability and an independent challenge to risk acceptance.

ctl.n: Payment message completeness and quality controls
ctl.ds: Rejects or queries payments with missing or meaningless party data, tracks deficiency rates and resubmissions and scorecards senders. It improves transparency of payment chains.

Sends requests for information to respondents or senders with deadlines, tracking of response quality and escalation of repeated deficiencies. It resolves unexplained activity and pressures partners to improve.

Alerts on repeated round-value or identical-value transactions by counterparty over a window. It is a supporting indicator of artificial, pre-arranged or structured flows and is best combined with other signals.

ctl.n: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
ctl.ds: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.

ctl.n: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
ctl.ds: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.

Verifies licences, registrations and supervisory status of customers, agents and counterparties against regulator registers before onboarding and periodically. It confirms legal authority to operate and detects unlicensed activity.
Obtains and verifies attestations and checks registers to confirm counterparties are not shell banks lacking physical presence and supervision. It bars a high-risk category of relationship outright.
Restricts payable-through access or requires customer due diligence and monitoring at the sub-account holder level. It ensures third parties using a correspondent account are known and supervised.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.
